note: Seed corpus shows the expected XPath expression format for the crypto:rc4_decrypt extension function.
Fuzzer passes the raw input bytes (the XSLT stylesheet) to the fuzzing harness.
The attacker-controlled input is parsed as an XSLT stylesheet, producing a stylesheet document.
The stylesheet is applied to the fixed xslt.xml input document; the crypto:rc4_decrypt template is evaluated.
The first argument (hex-encoded ciphertext) is popped from the XPath stack as a string.
The hex string is decoded into raw binary bytes; the length is stored in bin_len.
RC4 decryption is performed on the binary data, producing decrypted raw bytes that may contain invalid UTF-8 sequences.
The decrypted raw bytes are returned as an XML string without any UTF-8 validation, allowing invalid UTF-8 bytes to propagate into the result tree.
The result tree containing invalid UTF-8 bytes is serialized to a string.
Serialization writes the invalid UTF-8 bytes into the output buffer.
The output buffer content containing invalid UTF-8 is duplicated as a string.
The invalid UTF-8 bytes are appended to the XML buffer; the serializer's UTF-8 handling encounters the malformed sequence, triggering the memory-safety violation (crash) in the vulnerable target.
